questions.question: What does the stability-plasticity trade-off describe?
options: Balancing new learning with preservation of earlier capabilities
Balancing CPU usage with disk capacity
questions.explanation: Plasticity enables adaptation to new data, while stability prevents the update from erasing useful prior behavior.

questions.question: An update batch contains 100 examples and uses a 30% replay allocation. How many examples should come from retained tasks?
questions.explanation: A 30% replay allocation reserves 30 of the 100 examples for retained tasks and leaves 70 for recent data.

questions.question: A classifier adds new product categories while retaining every old category, and task identity is unavailable at inference time. Which scenario is this?
options: Task-incremental learning with a known task router
questions.explanation: Class-incremental learning expands the label set and requires one prediction space that still includes earlier classes.

questions.question: Why is performance on only the newest task an inadequate release metric?
options: It cannot reveal catastrophic forgetting on retained tasks
questions.explanation: A successful update must improve the new distribution without unacceptable regressions on earlier capabilities.

questions.question: A drift monitor fires during a seasonal event. What should happen before retraining starts?
options: Diagnose the change and validate labels, data contracts, and affected model slices
questions.explanation: A drift alert can represent expected seasonality, population movement, or broken instrumentation, so it must be diagnosed before adaptation.

questions.question: A canary model improves the new task but regresses a protected historical slice. Which release design gives the safest recovery?
options: Keep the candidate live until the next scheduled training run
Route all traffic to the candidate to collect more data
Restore the versioned previous checkpoint through a tested traffic rollback
Remove the historical slice from the release gate
questions.explanation: A versioned previous checkpoint and tested canary rollback contain exposure while the regression is diagnosed.
